question: What should the first OpenClaw-owned skill permission manifest contract include, and how should declared permissions relate to install consent, signing, attestation, ClawHub trust, and runtime enforcement?
rationale: The remaining work is a security boundary and public ecosystem contract; choosing schema placement, trust roots, consent semantics, and enforcement timing is not a safe autonomous cleanup decision.

options.title: Consolidate Design First
options.body: Keep this issue open as the product/security design anchor and use the related RFCs and PR as input before accepting a public manifest contract.

options.title: Land Audit-Only Metadata First
options.body: Adopt a narrow optional manifest that is clearly inspect-only, then track consent, signing, attestation, and enforcement as follow-up phases.

options.title: Route To ClawHub Policy
options.body: Make ClawHub or external governance plugins own declarations and trust scoring unless a missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Consolidate Design First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the product/security design anchor and use the related RFCs and PR as input before accepting a public manifest contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the latest human keep-open review and recent source-grounded docs work around the relevant skill and plugin-hook contracts.
